```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tan_2025_piperacillin_total"))$reference`
* Total piperacillin: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tan_2025_piperacillin_total"))$description`
* Unbound piperacillin: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tan_2025_piperacillin_unbound"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.01227-24> (open access; supplementary
  Tables S1-S2 and Figures S1-S9 in the article's supplemental material)

Tan 2025 fitted total and unbound (free) piperacillin concentrations from the
same samples as two separate population PK models with the same structure: two
compartments, allometric body-weight scaling to 70 kg, a bedside-Schwartz
creatinine clearance (CrCL) power effect on clearance, and inter-occasion
variability (IOV) on clearance for the pre- and post-operative periods. The
paper treats the total model as its primary analysis (Table 2) and uses the
unbound model (Table S2) for every dosing simulation. Both are packaged here.

# Population

Thirty-four critically ill children in the paediatric intensive care unit of
Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center who received prophylactic
piperacillin-tazobactam every 2-3 h around surgery (Table 1): median age 7.07
years (IQR 3.05-14.48), median weight 20.0 kg (IQR 12.65-55.33), 55.9% female,
median baseline bedside-Schwartz CrCL 143 mL/min/1.73 m^2 (IQR
102.81-181.53). Surgeries were liver transplantation (44.1%), total
pancreatectomy with islet auto-transplantation (5.9%), non-transplant abdominal
surgery (26.5%) and ear-nose-throat surgery (23.5%); median surgery duration
5.32 h. Patients under 45 kg received 80-90 mg/kg piperacillin and patients
over 45 kg 3000 or 4000 mg, as 30-min infusions. Scavenged opportunistic
sampling gave 286 total and 285 unbound concentrations (1-19 per patient).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Tan_2025_piperacillin_unbound")()$population`.

# Source trace

Both model files carry the per-parameter origin as an in-file comment. Values
for the total model come from Table 2 and for the unbound model from Table S2.

| Equation / parameter | Total (Table 2) | Unbound (Table S2) | Source location |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lcl` (CL, L/h/70 kg) | log(7.1) | log(8.95) | Table 2 / Table S2 |
| `lvc` (V1, L/70 kg) | log(17.2) | log(22.4) | Table 2 / Table S2 |
| `lq` (Q, L/h/70 kg) | log(3.25) | log(2.51) | Table 2 / Table S2 |
| `lvp` (V2, L/70 kg) | log(4.79) | log(4.48) | Table 2 / Table S2 |
| `e_crcl_cl` (CrCL exponent on CL) | 0.484 | 0.457 | Table 2 / Table S2 |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` (allometric exponents) | 0.75, 1 fixed | 0.75, 1 fixed | Methods, 'Population PK modeling'; Table S1 footnote 1 |
| `etalcl` (IIV CL) | 28.7% CV -> 0.07915 | 27.1% CV -> 0.07087 | Table 2 / Table S2, omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2) |
| `etalvc` (IIV V1) | 41% CV -> 0.15538 | 37.5% CV -> 0.13158 | Table 2 / Table S2 |
| `etaiov_cl_1` (IOV CL, preoperative) | 37.7% CV -> 0.13289 | 50.7% CV -> 0.22877 | Table 2 / Table S2 |
| `etaiov_cl_3` (IOV CL, postoperative) | 33.5% CV -> 0.10636 | 44.4% CV -> 0.17993 | Table 2 / Table S2 |
| `propSd` (proportional residual error) | 0.371 | 0.427 | Table 2 / Table S2 |
| CL = CL_pop (WT/70)^0.75 (CrCL/120)^theta | | | Results, final CL equation; Methods covariate equations |
| No IOV in the intraoperative period | | | Methods, IOV equation and text |
| IIV on Q and V2 fixed to 0 | | | Results, 'Population PK modeling' |
| Two-compartment, first-order elimination, IV infusion | | | Methods; Results |

# Typical-value check against the paper's simulations

The unbound model's typical clearance for the Figure 3 patient (20 kg, CrCL 143
mL/min/1.73 m^2) is `8.95 * (20/70)^0.75 * (143/120)^0.457` L/h. A continuous
infusion at steady state gives `Css = rate / CL`, and the medians that Figure 3
prints for its two continuous-infusion panels (read off the figure by the
maintainers: about 14.5 mg/L for 2.75 mg/kg/h and about 48.5 mg/L for 9.25
mg/kg/h) follow from it directly. This checks the CL, the allometric scaling and
the CrCL term of the packaged unbound model against the authors' own
simulation, without random effects.

```{r typical-css}
mod_free <- readModelDb("Tan_2025_piperacillin_unbound")
mod_tot <- readModelDb("Tan_2025_piperacillin_total")

ini_free <- rxode2::rxode(mod_free)$theta
cl_typ <- exp(ini_free[["lcl"]]) * (20 / 70)^0.75 * (143 / 120)^ini_free[["e_crcl_cl"]]

css_check <- tibble::tibble(
  regimen = c("10 mg/kg LD + 2.75 mg/kg/h", "20 mg/kg LD + 9.25 mg/kg/h"),
  rate_mg_h = c(2.75, 9.25) * 20,
  css_model = rate_mg_h / cl_typ,
  css_figure3 = c(14.5, 48.5)
) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (css_model - css_figure3) / css_figure3)

css_check |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen,
    "Infusion rate (mg/h)" = rate_mg_h,
    "Model Css (mg/L)" = css_model,
    "Figure 3 median (mg/L)" = css_figure3,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

# Digitised medians are read to about +/- 0.5 mg/L.
stopifnot(all(abs(css_check$pct_diff) < 5))
```

# Replicate Figure 3

Figure 3 simulates 1,000 virtual 20-kg patients with CrCL 143 mL/min/1.73 m^2
in the intraoperative period, which carries no IOV, under four regimens: 15
mg/kg and 55 mg/kg every 2 h as 30-min infusions, and a 10 or 20 mg/kg 30-min
loading dose followed immediately by a 2.75 or 9.25 mg/kg/h continuous
infusion. The bands are reproduced here with 200 virtual patients per regimen
and without residual error; the paper's continuous-infusion 5th-95th
percentile bands (about 9.5-23 mg/L and 32-77 mg/L at steady state) match the
spread that between-subject variability on CL alone produces, so residual
error was evidently not added to the plotted bands.

```{r fig3-sim}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20250303)
n_per_arm <- 200
wt_fig <- 20
crcl_fig <- 143

regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,                                ~type, ~dose_mgkg, ~rate_mgkgh,
  "Q2H 15 mg/kg (1x MIC)",                 "q2h", 15,         NA,
  "LD 10 mg/kg + CI 2.75 mg/kg/h (1x MIC)", "ci",  10,         2.75,
  "Q2H 55 mg/kg (4x MIC)",                 "q2h", 55,         NA,
  "LD 20 mg/kg + CI 9.25 mg/kg/h (4x MIC)", "ci",  20,         9.25
) |>
  mutate(regimen = factor(regimen, levels = regimen))

fig3_times <- sort(unique(round(c(seq(0, 24, by = 0.1), seq(0.5, 24, by = 2)), 2)))

make_events <- function(reg_row, ids, wt, crcl, times, t_end = max(times)) {
  dose_mg <- reg_row$dose_mgkg * wt
  if (reg_row$type == "q2h") {
    dosing <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = seq(0, t_end - 2, by = 2)) |>
      mutate(amt = dose_mg[match(id, ids)], rate = amt / 0.5)
  } else {
    ld <- tibble::tibble(id = ids, time = 0, amt = dose_mg, rate = amt / 0.5)
    ci_rate <- reg_row$rate_mgkgh * wt
    ci <- tibble::tibble(id = ids, time = 0.5, rate = ci_rate, amt = ci_rate * (t_end - 0.5))
    dosing <- bind_rows(ld, ci)
  }
  dosing <- dosing |> mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "central")
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(dosing, obs) |>
    left_join(tibble::tibble(id = ids, WT = wt, CRCL = crcl), by = "id") |>
    mutate(OCC = 2L, regimen = as.character(reg_row$regimen)) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

ev_fig3 <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  ids <- (i - 1) * n_per_arm + seq_len(n_per_arm)
  make_events(regimens[i, ], ids, rep(wt_fig, n_per_arm), rep(crcl_fig, n_per_arm), times = fig3_times)
}))

sim_fig3 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_free, events = ev_fig3, keep = "regimen", returnType = "data.frame")

band_fig3 <- sim_fig3 |>
  group_by(regimen, time) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), p50 = median(Cc), p95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r fig3-plot, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3 of Tan 2025: simulated unbound piperacillin in 20-kg patients with CrCL 143 mL/min/1.73 m^2. Black line, median; shaded band, 5th-95th percentiles; dashed red line, the 8 mg/L (1x MIC) or 32 mg/L (4x MIC) target."}
targets <- tibble::tibble(
  regimen = factor(levels(regimens$regimen), levels = levels(regimens$regimen)),
  target = c(8, 8, 32, 32)
)
ggplot(band_fig3, aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), fill = "grey70") +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(data = targets, aes(yintercept = target), colour = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~regimen, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Unbound piperacillin (mg/L)") +
  theme_bw()
```

The maintainers read the medians and band edges below off Figure 3. They are
compared with the simulated medians at the same times; the first-dose trough
of the 15 mg/kg regimen, the steady-state peak and trough of both Q2H regimens,
and the steady-state plateau of both infusions are all reproduced.

```{r fig3-compare}
fig3_digitised <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,                                ~time, ~what,                       ~fig3,
  "Q2H 15 mg/kg (1x MIC)",                 0.5,   "first peak",                38.5,
  "Q2H 15 mg/kg (1x MIC)",                 2,     "first trough",              14,
  "Q2H 15 mg/kg (1x MIC)",                 22.5,  "steady-state peak",         59.5,
  "Q2H 15 mg/kg (1x MIC)",                 24,    "steady-state trough",       25,
  "Q2H 55 mg/kg (4x MIC)",                 0.5,   "first peak",                140,
  "Q2H 55 mg/kg (4x MIC)",                 22.5,  "steady-state peak",         219,
  "Q2H 55 mg/kg (4x MIC)",                 24,    "steady-state trough",       91,
  "LD 10 mg/kg + CI 2.75 mg/kg/h (1x MIC)", 0.5,   "end of loading dose",       25.5,
  "LD 10 mg/kg + CI 2.75 mg/kg/h (1x MIC)", 24,    "plateau",                   14.5,
  "LD 20 mg/kg + CI 9.25 mg/kg/h (4x MIC)", 0.5,   "end of loading dose",       51,
  "LD 20 mg/kg + CI 9.25 mg/kg/h (4x MIC)", 24,    "plateau",                   48.5
)

fig3_cmp <- fig3_digitised |>
  left_join(
    band_fig3 |> mutate(regimen = as.character(regimen), time = round(time, 2)),
    by = c("regimen", "time")
  ) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (p50 - fig3) / fig3)

fig3_cmp |>
  select(regimen, what, time, fig3, p50, pct_diff) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen, "Point" = what, "Time (h)" = time,
    "Figure 3 median (mg/L)" = fig3, "Simulated median (mg/L)" = p50,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

stopifnot(
  # A transcription error in CL, V1 or the covariate exponents shifts every
  # point by tens of percent; digitising error is a few percent.
  abs(median(fig3_cmp$pct_diff)) < 5,
  quantile(abs(fig3_cmp$pct_diff), 0.9) < 12
)
```

# Replicate the Table 3 and Table 4 dosing recommendations

Tables 3 and 4 give, for each of five CrCL bands and four body-weight bands, the
lowest dose at which more than 90% of virtual patients keep unbound
piperacillin above the target (8 mg/L for 1x MIC, 32 mg/L for 4x MIC) for the
whole intraoperative period. For Q2H dosing the criterion is the first trough
(2 h); for continuous infusion it is the concentration over the surgery once
the loading dose has been given. Covariates were drawn uniformly within each
band (the open-ended bands as 70-89 kg and 130-159 mL/min/1.73 m^2, per the
Methods). The continuous-infusion criterion is evaluated here as the minimum
concentration from the end of the loading dose (0.5 h) to 8 h, which covers the
cohort's surgery durations (median 5.32 h, IQR 2.93-8.89).

```{r tables34-setup}
wt_bands <- tibble::tribble(
  ~wt_band,   ~wt_lo, ~wt_hi,
  "10-29 kg", 10,     29,
  "30-49 kg", 30,     49,
  "50-69 kg", 50,     69,
  ">=70 kg",  70,     89
)
crcl_bands <- tibble::tribble(
  ~crcl_band, ~crcl_lo, ~crcl_hi,
  "20-29",    20,       29,
  "30-59",    30,       59,
  "60-89",    60,       89,
  "90-129",   90,       129,
  ">=130",    130,      159
)

# Table 3 (Q2H, mg/kg) and Table 4 (continuous infusion, mg/kg/h after a
# 10 or 20 mg/kg loading dose); rows CrCL band, columns weight band.
tab3_1x <- c(7.5, 7, 6.5, 6, 9, 8.5, 8, 7.5, 9.5, 9, 8.5, 8, 10.5, 10, 9.5, 9, 15, 11, 10.5, 10)
tab3_4x <- c(29, 27, 25, 25, 30, 30, 30, 30, 40, 38, 36, 34, 41, 39, 37, 35, 55, 45, 43, 41)
tab4_1x <- c(1.25, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2.5, 2.25, 2.25, 2, 2.75, 2.5, 2.25, 2)
tab4_4x <- c(4.25, 4.25, 4.25, 3.25, 6, 6, 6, 6, 7.5, 6, 6, 6, 9, 7.5, 6, 6, 9.25, 7.75, 7.5, 6.5)

cells <- tidyr::expand_grid(crcl_band = crcl_bands$crcl_band, wt_band = wt_bands$wt_band) |>
  left_join(crcl_bands, by = "crcl_band") |>
  left_join(wt_bands, by = "wt_band")

recs <- bind_rows(
  cells |> mutate(target = 8, type = "q2h", dose_mgkg = tab3_1x, rate_mgkgh = NA_real_),
  cells |> mutate(target = 32, type = "q2h", dose_mgkg = tab3_4x, rate_mgkgh = NA_real_),
  cells |> mutate(target = 8, type = "ci", dose_mgkg = 10, rate_mgkgh = tab4_1x),
  cells |> mutate(target = 32, type = "ci", dose_mgkg = 20, rate_mgkgh = tab4_4x)
) |>
  mutate(cell = row_number(), regimen = as.character(cell))
nrow(recs)
```

```{r tables34-sim}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20250304)
n_cell <- 200
tab_times <- seq(0, 8, by = 0.25)

ev_tab <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(recs)), function(i) {
  r <- recs[i, ]
  ids <- (i - 1) * n_cell + seq_len(n_cell)
  make_events(
    r, ids,
    wt = stats::runif(n_cell, r$wt_lo, r$wt_hi),
    crcl = stats::runif(n_cell, r$crcl_lo, r$crcl_hi),
    times = tab_times
  ) |> mutate(cell = r$cell)
}))

sim_tab <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_free, events = ev_tab, keep = "cell", returnType = "data.frame")

pta <- sim_tab |>
  left_join(recs |> select(cell, type, target), by = "cell") |>
  filter((type == "q2h" & abs(time - 2) < 1e-8) | (type == "ci" & time >= 0.5)) |>
  group_by(cell, id) |>
  summarise(cmin = min(Cc), target = first(target), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(cell) |>
  summarise(pta = 100 * mean(cmin > target), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(recs, by = "cell")
```

```{r tables34-show}
pta_wide <- pta |>
  mutate(
    criterion = paste0(ifelse(type == "q2h", "Q2H", "CI"), " ", ifelse(target == 8, "1x", "4x"), " MIC"),
    wt_band = factor(wt_band, levels = wt_bands$wt_band),
    crcl_band = factor(crcl_band, levels = crcl_bands$crcl_band)
  ) |>
  select(criterion, crcl_band, wt_band, pta) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = wt_band, values_from = pta) |>
  arrange(criterion, crcl_band)

pta_wide |>
  dplyr::rename("Criterion" = criterion, "CrCL (mL/min/1.73 m^2)" = crcl_band) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0, caption = "Percentage of 200 virtual patients per cell meeting the target at the Table 3 / Table 4 recommended dose.")

pta_summary <- pta |>
  group_by(type, target) |>
  summarise(median_pta = median(pta), p10_pta = quantile(pta, 0.1), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(pta_summary, digits = 1)
```

The recommended doses were chosen as the lowest that exceed 90% attainment, so
in a faithful reproduction the attainment of a recommended dose sits at or
somewhat above 90%; doses were stepped in coarse increments, so some cells
overshoot, and with 200 virtual patients per cell a cell's attainment carries a
sampling error of about 2 percentage points. Across the 80 cells the simulated
attainment ranges from `r round(min(pta$pta))`% to `r round(max(pta$pta))`%.

```{r tables34-assert}
stopifnot(
  # Centre: the recommended doses hit the paper's >90% criterion.
  all(pta_summary$median_pta > 88),
  # Envelope: robust to which cells land in the tails of a 200-patient draw.
  all(pta_summary$p10_pta > 80)
)
```

# Inter-occasion variability by surgical period

The intraoperative period is the zero-IOV reference; the pre- and
post-operative periods each draw their own eta on CL. Simulating the same
virtual patients in each period shows the spread that the IOV adds to the
individual clearance (both models).

```{r iov}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20250305)
n_iov <- 200
iov_ev <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_len(n_iov), OCC = 1:3) |>
  mutate(time = 0, evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", WT = 20, CRCL = 143) |>
  mutate(id = (OCC - 1L) * n_iov + id)

iov_cl <- bind_rows(
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_tot, events = iov_ev, keep = "OCC", returnType = "data.frame") |>
    mutate(model = "Total"),
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_free, events = iov_ev, keep = "OCC", returnType = "data.frame") |>
    mutate(model = "Unbound")
) |>
  mutate(period = factor(OCC, levels = 1:3, labels = c("Preoperative", "Intraoperative", "Postoperative")))

iov_cl |>
  group_by(model, period) |>
  summarise(median_cl = median(cl), cv_pct = 100 * sd(log(cl)), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Model" = model, "Period" = period,
    "Median CL (L/h)" = median_cl, "SD of log CL x 100" = cv_pct
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

# PKNCA on the Figure 3 Q2H regimens

The paper reports no NCA, so PKNCA is used here to summarise the simulated
unbound exposure of the two Figure 3 Q2H regimens: the first dosing interval
(0-2 h) and the last (22-24 h, near steady state). The accumulation from the
first to the last interval (an AUC ratio of about 1.7) reflects a terminal
half-life of about 1.7 h for the typical 20-kg patient, close to the 2-h dosing
interval.

```{r pknca}
q2h_sim <- sim_fig3 |>
  filter(grepl("^Q2H", regimen)) |>
  mutate(treatment = as.character(regimen)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc))

q2h_dose <- ev_fig3 |>
  filter(evid == 1, grepl("^Q2H", regimen)) |>
  mutate(treatment = as.character(regimen)) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(q2h_sim, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(q2h_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 22), end = c(2, 24),
  cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_summary <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast")) |>
  group_by(treatment, start, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)

nca_summary |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = treatment, "Interval start (h)" = start,
    "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax, "AUC over the 2-h interval (mg*h/L)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

# Linear model: the 55 mg/kg regimen is exactly 55/15 times the 15 mg/kg one
# for the same patients' covariates; random draws differ, so compare centres.
ratio <- nca_summary$auclast[grepl("55", nca_summary$treatment)] /
  nca_summary$auclast[grepl("15", nca_summary$treatment)]
stopifnot(all(abs(ratio / (55 / 15) - 1) < 0.1))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **CV% to variance.** Tables 2 and S2 report IIV and IOV as CV%. The packaged
  variances use `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`. The paper does not state its
  conversion; for CVs of 27-51% the alternative reading `omega = CV` gives
  variances 0.6-12% larger, which the Figure 3 bands cannot distinguish.
* **Occasion coding.** The paper defines three surgical periods with no IOV in
  the intraoperative one and separately estimated IOV variances for the pre-
  and post-operative ones. This is encoded as `OCC` = 1 (preoperative), 2
  (intraoperative) and 3 (postoperative), with one eta per non-reference
  period. Each patient has at most one occasion of each kind, so one draw per
  period per patient is equivalent to NONMEM's per-occasion eta. Because the
  etas enter clearance through occasion indicators, rxode2 warns that they are
  not mu-referenced; this affects only estimation speed-ups, not simulation.
* **CrCL reference.** CL is scaled by `(CrCL/120)^theta`, with 120
  mL/min/1.73 m^2 the "median value ... in the general population" stated in
  the Methods, not the cohort median (143). The typical CL in each model
  therefore refers to a 70-kg patient with CrCL 120 mL/min/1.73 m^2. The paper
  does not say whether CrCL was time-varying in the fit; the dosing
  simulations hold it constant.
* **Residual error.** Only a proportional residual error was retained (Methods;
  RSE printed as 0% in both tables). The Figure 3 and Table 3/4 replications
  here use individual predictions without residual error, consistent with the
  width of the paper's bands.
* **Table 3/4 reproduction.** The paper does not state how covariates were
  sampled within a band or the exact window over which the continuous-infusion
  criterion was evaluated. Uniform draws within each band and the 0.5-8 h
  window are the maintainers' choices; the Methods also list a "90-119" CrCL
  band while Tables 3-4 print "90-129", and the table bands are used.
* **Covariates screened but not retained** (postmenstrual age and each surgery
  type, Table S1) are recorded in `covariatesDataExcluded` and are not in the
  models.
